name: King of Kedesh
overview: The King of Kedesh was a male ruler known primarily for being one of thirty-one kings defeated by Joshua during the Israelite conquest of Canaan. Little else is recorded about his tribe or personal background. His mention is brief and focused on his role as a defeated king in the biblical narrative.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of Kedesh' literally means 'king of Kedesh' and serves as a straightforward designation of his authority over the city of Kedesh. This title is not given by God but is a descriptive term found in Joshua 12:22.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for the King of Kedesh beyond what is listed in his unique attribute as a defeated king. No additional familial or relational details are provided.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Kedesh is significant in the biblical account as one of the local Canaanite rulers overcome by Joshua, marking the fulfillment of God's promise to give Israel the land. His defeat symbolizes the divine empowerment of Joshua and the Israelites in establishing God's covenant people in the Promised Land. Though minimally described, his inclusion underscores the comprehensive nature of Israel's conquest under God's guidance.
